**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (fill: $223.00, ~$9,812 total).

**Summary — what I did and why:** I researched Apple's most recent results and news, then bought a starter AAPL position of 44 shares at $223.00 (≈$9,812), which sits inside my mandate: AAPL-only buy, under the $10,000 per-order cap, under the $20,000 daily cap (this was the day's only trade), a limit price essentially at the market (quote was $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask), and no funds withdrawn from the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and the 2024-10-31 earnings release, which showed full-year net sales of $391.035B, net income of $93.736B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (the year included a one-time $10.2B tax charge), with Q4 revenue of $94.9B up 6% year over year — a return to growth after prior-year declines. Recent news flow was mild and mixed (shares "little changed at about $222" as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout), which argues for a measured position rather than a full-size one. One caveat on process: a low-quality aggregator site ("finance-summaries.net") surfaced in search results claiming FY2024 revenue of $416.2B, net income of $112.0B and EPS of $7.46; I disregarded those numbers because they conflict with both Apple's own newsroom release and the SEC filing, and I relied only on the verified $391.0B / $93.7B / $6.08 figures.
